title: Flat strict transforms are their generic closures
statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be integral Noetherian schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), with generic points $\eta$ and $\eta_T$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $v:T\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism over a nonempty open $U\subset S$. Let $X\to S$ be a dominant finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $X$ integral, and let $H\subset X$ be the schematic closure [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] of a closed subscheme $H_\eta\subset X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-closed-immersion], possibly empty. Write $X'$ and $H'$ for the schematic closures of $X_U\times_U v^{-1}(U)$ and $H_U\times_U v^{-1}(U)$ in $X\times_S T$ and $H\times_S T$, respectively [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that $X'\to T$ and $H'\to T$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then their generic fibres identify with $X_\eta$ and $H_\eta$ over the canonical residue-field isomorphism $\kappa(\eta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\eta_T)$ [def-weil-residue-field] induced by $v$. Each generic fibre is topologically and schematically dense in its transform; that is, local functions are determined by restriction to it. Consequently, inside $X\times_S T$, $X'$ and $H'$ are precisely the schematic closures of $X_\eta\times_S T$ and $H_\eta\times_S T$. The scheme $X'$ is integral, $H'$ is a closed subscheme of $X'$, and $X'\to X$ is proper and an isomorphism over the dense open $X_U$, hence birational (the two integral schemes have isomorphic dense open subschemes via this projection).

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform, schematic-closure description; ILO Expose X Theorem 3.4, paragraph before the proof and Step 2, printed p.160. Flat generic-density and integrality argument supplied in retained parent proof Steps 5--6.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_S T$ and $W_H=H\times_S T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $W\to X$ is proper. In particular it is finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] first to $X\to S$ and then to $W\to X$: both $X$ and $W$ are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $W_H\to W$ is a closed immersion. Here the Noetherian convention in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact: by [pqf-def-locnoeth] choose an affine cover of $W$ with Noetherian coordinate rings, and use quasi-compactness to extract a finite subcover. Conversely the finite affine-cover convention in our hypotheses implies these two properties, since affine schemes are quasi-compact and a finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact. By [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] each chart is a Noetherian space, and by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] every subset of each chart is quasi-compact. Every subset of $W$ is consequently quasi-compact: restrict any open cover to these finitely many chart intersections and unite the finite subcovers. This also applies to every subset of $W_H$. Thus the open immersions $W_U\to W$ and $(W_H)_U\to W_H$ are quasi-compact: their inverse images of affine opens are subsets of the spaces just considered. Consequently the quasi-compact kernel description of schematic image in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] applies to both transforms.

proof.text: First the closure $H$ has the prescribed generic fibre: on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, put $K=\kappa(\eta)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. The given closed subscheme has ideal $J\subset B\otimes_A K=B_{A\setminus\{0\}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its map to this affine of $X$ is a map of affine schemes, hence quasi-compact. The kernel formula of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] therefore gives the closure ideal $I=\ker(B\to B_{A\setminus\{0\}}/J)$, the contraction of $J$. Then $IB_{A\setminus\{0\}}=J$: if $b/s\in J$, multiplication by the unit $s$ gives $b/1\in J$, hence $b\in I$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. This proves $H\times_S\eta=H_\eta$, using the fractions in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. On the open $W_U$, restriction of $\ker(\mathcal O_W\to j_*\mathcal O_{W_U})$ is zero, because the restricted map is the identity. Hence $X'_U=W_U\simeq X_U$. The identical calculation inside $W_H$ gives $H'_U\simeq H_U$. Since $U$ is nonempty in integral $S$, it contains $\eta$. The isomorphism $v^{-1}U\simeq U$ sends $\eta_T$ to $\eta$ and induces the specified residue-field isomorphism. By the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-scheme-fibre], base change of these open identifications to that point gives $X'_{\eta_T}\simeq X_\eta$ and $H'_{\eta_T}\simeq H_\eta$, compatibly with their maps into $W$. Also $X_\eta\times_S T\simeq X'_{\eta_T}$ and $H_\eta\times_S T\simeq H'_{\eta_T}$, since $T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta_T)$.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), restriction of its kernel formula to the original open; generic base change through that open. Generic localization and contraction-extension of ideals, using Schemes Tags 01I4 and 01JQ, Morphisms Tag 01RV, and Algebra Tag 07JZ.

proof.text: Let $Y$ be either $X'$ or $H'$. For every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$ mapping into a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ a flat $A$-module. The ring $A$ is a domain, and [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $K=\kappa(\eta_T)$ with its fraction field. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], $ab=0$ with $0\ne a\in A$ implies $b=0$. The affine fibre formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the generic restriction with $B\to B\otimes_A K$. This tensor product is the localization of $B$ at $A\setminus\{0\}$: the mutually inverse maps send $b\otimes(a/s)$ to $ab/s$ and $b/s$ to $b\otimes(1/s)$. By the fraction equivalence relation in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $b/1=0$ means $ab=0$ for some nonzero $a\in A$, so this restriction is injective. Such affine opens cover every open of $Y$. A local section restricting to zero on the generic fibre is therefore zero on this affine cover and hence zero. Thus $\mathcal O_Y\to(i_Y)_*\mathcal O_{Y_{\eta_T}}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); More on Algebra Tag 0538 (lemma-flat-torsion-free); Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); Schemes Tags 01I4 and 01JQ (affine fibre products); Algebra Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module).

proof.text: The morphism $i_Y:Y_{\eta_T}\to Y$ is quasi-compact: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over an affine open of $T$ its inverse image is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A K)$ from Step 3. For an arbitrary affine open of $Y$, cover it by finitely many such affine subopens (it is quasi-compact), so its inverse image is again quasi-compact. The zero kernel from Step 3 means $\operatorname{SIm}(i_Y)=Y$ by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], the closure of its topological range is all of $Y$, giving topological density too. Inside $W$ the kernel of restriction to $X'$ equals the kernel of restriction to $X'_{\eta_T}$, because restriction on $X'$ is injective. The generic-fibre map to $W$ is also quasi-compact: over an affine open of $W$ mapping into an affine of $T$, its preimage is the generic fibre of the affine closed subscheme cut out by $X'$. Thus these are the quasi-coherent restriction kernels defining the schematic images, and their schematic images in $W$ agree. The same holds for $H'$ inside $W_H$, and also inside $W$, since $W_H$ is closed there. Together with Step 2 these are exactly the two asserted generic-closure equalities. This argument works for the empty scheme as well: its structure sheaf is zero and its closure is empty.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), parts (1), (2), (4), and comparison of the restriction kernels.

proof.text: We verify the closed inclusion scheme-theoretically. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset W$, write $W_H\cap\operatorname{Spec}R=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$, using the closed immersion of Step 1 and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ideal of $X'$ is the kernel of restriction from $R$ to $W_U\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$. The inverse image in $R$ of the ideal defining $H'$ in $R/J$ is the kernel of restriction from $R$ to $(W_H)_U\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$. The latter restriction factors through the former, so the first kernel is contained in the second. These inclusions on affine opens identify $H'$ with a closed subscheme of $X'$. This uses the schematic restriction kernels, rather than an inclusion of underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), kernel formula; Tag 01QO (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion), affine quotient description.

proof.text: Dominance of $X\to S$ implies $X_U\ne\varnothing$. As a nonempty open of integral $X$, it is reduced and irreducible. Its isomorphic copy $W_U$ is reduced; [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] therefore identifies $X'$ with the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|W_U|}$ in $W$. This closure is nonempty and irreducible (the closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible). Hence $X'$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Finally $X'\to W\to X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], clause (b), using Step 1. Its restriction over $X_U$ is the isomorphism of Step 2. The open $X_U$ is dense in integral $X$; its inverse image $W_U$ is dense in $X'$ by the closure description just used. Thus this projection identifies dense opens of the two integral schemes and is birational, as asserted.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q34-045c0432a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item and all six steps in full. There are no new nodes and no fixes. The statement changes from the live unsplit base are clarifications only: (1) Noetherian is spelled out as a finite Noetherian affine cover, which is equivalent to locally Noetherian plus quasi-compact; (2) the residue-field equality becomes the isomorphism induced by v, and def-weil-residue-field is added; (3) birational is spelled out. No hypothesis was added or dropped and no conclusion weakened, and the parent flatification-horizontal-curve-pair Step 3 uses exactly these hypotheses and conclusions. This re-delivery of 51807634 (previously approved, then refused at landing) is not identical: Step 1 now cites pqf-def-locnoeth and Step 2 states the quasi-compactness behind the kernel formula. S1: proper base change and 01T6 twice make W Noetherian; with 00FQ and 04ZA every subset is quasi-compact, so W_U→W and (W_H)_U→W_H are quasi-compact open immersions and the kernel description of the image applies; W_H→W is a closed immersion. S2: on affine charts the closure ideal I of H_eta is the contraction of J, and I·B_K=J, so H×η=H_eta. The kernel vanishes on W_U, so X'_U≅X_U and H'_U≅H_U. T×_S κ(η)=κ(η_T) gives the generic-fibre identifications. S3: flatness over a domain gives torsion-freeness (0538), and B→B⊗K=B_{A∖0} is injective; this is the only use of flatness. S4: the generic fibre has kernel 0, so it is schematically dense; the support clause gives topological density; left exactness of the pushforward gives the closures in W, and in W_H for H'. S5: the restriction kernels give H'⊂X' as schemes, in the correct direction. S6: 056B gives the reduced induced structure on an irreducible closure, so X' is integral; it is proper by clause (b) of the closed-immersion-proper node; and X'→X is an isomorphism over X_U with W_U dense, hence birational. Sources checked: Stacks 01R8, 056B, 0538, 01U5, and ILO X Thm 3.4 Step 2, printed p.160 ('proper transforms will coincide with the base changes'). The proof is correctly marked agent-written, and no SGA source is used. Edge cases tested: v=id, empty H_eta, nonreduced K[x]/(x^2), dim S≥2, and nonflat A/(t). Duplicate search found only a field-based equivariant variant (lem-sfb-flat-generic-closure-equivariance), a dense-integral-open criterion and the Chow closure node; none restates the item.
